title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree All Classes Benefiting From It And The Derivation Of Sciences And Sharia From It

questions.question: What does the passage say about who can benefit from the Qur'an's teaching?
questions.answer: People of every level, from the least educated to the most learned, can benefit from it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about understanding deep truths in the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It says people are able to grasp its deep meanings according to their share and ability.

questions.question: Which kinds of scholars are mentioned as taking knowledge from the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Experts in Islamic law, many Islamic sciences, and scholars of belief and religion are mentioned.

questions.question: What does the passage compare the Qur'an to when speaking about truth and reality?
questions.answer: It compares it to a source and a rich mine.

questions.question: Why is the silence of non-Muslim Arab literary experts important in the passage?
questions.answer: Because they were very skilled in language and had a strong reason to challenge the Qur'an, yet they could not match it.

questions.question: What small part of the Qur'an does the passage say others could not produce anything like?
questions.answer: They could not produce anything equal even to one surah.

questions.question: Is eloquence presented as the only miraculous side of the Qur'an or just one of them?
questions.answer: It is presented as only one side among several major sides.

questions.question: What does the failure of speakers and scholars through history show, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that the Qur'an is beyond human power to copy or defeat.

questions.question: What main idea is given in the first paragraph of the target passage about the Qur'an and human learning?
questions.answer: The Qur'an teaches all kinds of people and gives scholars what they need in their fields.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the Qur'an speaks to both simple and advanced minds?
questions.answer: It says everyone, from the weakest in understanding to the strongest, receives a share from it.

questions.question: What is the meaning of calling the Qur'an a “mine of reality” in this passage?
questions.answer: It means it is full of true knowledge waiting to be discovered.

questions.question: Why were Arab experts in language especially important as a test of the Qur'an's literary power?
questions.answer: Because they were the strongest people in language and would have challenged it if they could.

questions.question: What did those literary experts fail to do?
questions.answer: They failed to bring even one chapter like it.

questions.question: What does their failure suggest about the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It suggests that its excellence is miraculous and not something humans can reach.

questions.question: Are only ancient people mentioned as unable to challenge the Qur'an?
questions.answer: No, later speakers and scholars are also mentioned.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention people who wanted fame by opposing the Qur'an?
questions.answer: To show that even people with strong motivation still could not defeat it.

questions.question: According to the passage, do only scholars understand the Qur'an? Explain.
questions.answer: No. Ordinary people and scholars both benefit from it, each according to their level.

questions.question: What does the passage say scholars of different Islamic subjects find in the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They find the needed principles, answers, and knowledge for their subjects.

questions.question: Why does this wide benefit act like a sign for the Qur'an's truth?
questions.answer: Because one book guiding so many levels and sciences points to a special and true source.

questions.question: Which group is described as highly skilled in literature but still unable to answer the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Non-Muslim Arab literary masters are described that way.

questions.question: Why is their inability to match it a strong proof in the passage?
questions.answer: Because they were the most able in language and also had a reason to oppose it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about matching just one surah?
questions.answer: It says they could not do even that.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the reaction of later famous speakers and scholars who opposed it?
questions.answer: They ended up unable to answer it and stayed powerless before it.

questions.question: What does this teach about human power compared with the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It teaches that human skill cannot reach its level.

questions.question: What overall judgment does the passage make about the Qur'an after mentioning these studies?
questions.answer: It judges the Qur'an to be peerless, miraculous, and a marvel.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the range of people who take lessons from the Qur'an?
questions.answer: It describes a very wide range, including the simplest people and the most knowledgeable.

questions.question: What does this wide range suggest about the Qur'an's message?
questions.answer: It suggests that its guidance is broad, deep, and suitable for all people.

questions.question: Which areas of Islamic study are said to draw from the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Islamic law, many religious sciences, theology, and the foundations of belief are said to draw from it.

questions.question: What picture does the passage use to show that the Qur'an contains many truths?
questions.answer: It uses the picture of a rich place full of valuable treasure.

questions.question: Who are described as the strongest literary challengers in the passage?
questions.answer: The Arab masters of language who did not accept Islam are described that way.

questions.question: Why would those challengers have wanted to answer the Qur'an if they could?
questions.answer: Because they needed to oppose it and would have gained by doing so.

questions.question: What specific challenge could they not meet?
questions.answer: They could not bring something equal even to a single chapter.

questions.question: What does the passage say about eloquence compared with the Qur'an's other miraculous qualities?
questions.answer: It says eloquence is only one part among its major miraculous qualities.

questions.question: What happened to later people who tried to challenge the Qur'an for fame?
questions.answer: They were still unable to answer even one aspect of it.

questions.question: What do all these examples act as a stamp or sign for?
questions.answer: They act as a sign that the Qur'an is unmatched and miraculous.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about how different people understand the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Different people understand from it according to their level, but all can benefit.

questions.question: Why is this important for understanding the Qur'an's greatness?
questions.answer: Because one book helping all levels of people shows unusual wisdom and truth.

questions.question: What kinds of scholars are said to take answers from the Qur'an for their own studies?
questions.answer: Scholars of Islamic law, theology, and many branches of Islamic knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying the Qur'an is a source of truth?
questions.answer: It means true guidance and real knowledge come from it.

questions.question: Which group had great language skill but still could not answer the Qur'an?
questions.answer: Non-Muslim Arab experts in literature and speech.

questions.question: Why does their failure matter more than the failure of ordinary people?
questions.answer: Because they were the best trained and most able in that field.

questions.question: What is one clear sign in the passage that the Qur'an is beyond human ability?
questions.answer: Even one surah could not be matched by its challengers.

questions.question: What does the passage show by mentioning famous speakers until modern times?
questions.answer: It shows that the challenge remained unanswered across history.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur'an's teaching for people with different abilities?
questions.answer: It says everyone can take a proper share from its teaching, no matter their level.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Qur'an to many branches of Islamic knowledge?
questions.answer: It says scholars in many fields draw their needed knowledge and answers from it.

questions.question: What does that tell us about the Qur'an as a book?
questions.answer: It tells us that it is rich, dependable, and full of truth.

questions.question: Who were the strongest language experts mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: Arab literary masters who did not believe in the Qur'an.

questions.question: What chance did they have to challenge the Qur'an?
questions.answer: They had the skill and the reason to challenge it, but they still failed.

questions.question: What was the smallest unit they could not match?
questions.answer: They could not match even a single surah.

questions.question: Is the Qur'an's literary beauty described as all of its miracle or only part of it?
questions.answer: Only part of it.

questions.question: What happened to later scholars and orators who tried to oppose it?
questions.answer: They could not challenge any part of its miraculous nature.

questions.question: What does all of this become a sign of?
questions.answer: It becomes a sign that the Qur'an is matchless and miraculous.
